title: Tempo Run with Dynamic Activation - Engelbrektsloppet Prep

items.name: Cat-Cow
items.cues: Move slowly and deliberately, synchronizing breath with movement. Arch on inhale, round on exhale to mobilize the spine.

items.name: 90/90 Hip Switches
items.cues: Control the switching motion, keeping your torso upright. Feel the external rotation and mobility in each hip position.

items.name: Bird Dog
items.cues: Extend opposite arm and leg fully, maintaining a neutral spine. Hold each rep for 1 second and avoid rotating your hips.

items.name: Light Treadmill or Track Jog
items.cues: Easy conversational pace, focus on relaxed form and getting your body temperature up gradually.

items.name: Tempo Run - Progressive Build
items.cues: Start at a comfortably hard pace (RPE 6). After 10 minutes, increase to sustained tempo pace (RPE 7-8). Maintain steady breathing—aim for 3 counts in, 3 counts out. Focus on consistent turnover and efficient ground contact. This is an aerobic workout designed to improve lactate threshold, critical for the 45km Engelbrektsloppet. Monitor your effort carefully; you should be able to speak only short sentences.

items.name: Light Recovery Jog
items.cues: Easy pace, bring heart rate down gradually. This active recovery aids lactate clearance and promotes blood flow.

items.name: Calf Stretch
items.cues: Hold each leg at the wall or bar. Keep your heel down and lean forward until you feel a gentle stretch. Breathe deeply.

items.name: Biceps Wall Stretch
items.cues: Stand facing a wall with arm extended and palm up. Gently rotate your body away to increase the stretch. Hold for 30 seconds each side.

items.name: Static Standing Quad Stretch
items.cues: Pull your foot toward your glute, keeping your knee aligned under your hip. Hold for 30 seconds each leg without bouncing.

items.name: Cat-Cow
items.cues: Gentle, easy movements to promote spinal mobility and aid recovery. Move with your breath and relax the nervous system.

rationale: Tempo workout targets lactate threshold development, essential for ultramarathon performance over 45km. RPE 7-8 provides the right intensity window to improve aerobic capacity without overtraining with 20 days until race.

Recent training shows consistent endurance work; this tempo session adds intensity variation while respecting the athlete's 'great' current status. Progressive build structure allows the body to adapt gradually.
Includes activation patterns (Cat-Cow, 90/90 Hip Switches, Bird Dog) from recent sessions to maintain mobility and neuromuscular coordination before the harder running effort.
